- **Database**: PostgreSQL via Prisma ORM
- **Styling**: Tailwind CSS + shadcn/ui
- **Charts**: Recharts

[mcp-huly/PROJECT.md#ECDF]
1:# mcp-huly — Project Overview
2:
3:## Ringkasan
4:
5:`mcp-huly` adalah MCP (Model Context Protocol) server yang menjembatani
6:Claude (atau MCP client lain) dengan instance Huly self-hosted milik QTI
7:(`huly.qti.co.id`). Tujuannya: memungkinkan Claude membaca dan mengelola
8:project, issue, milestone, document, test run, anggota tim, dan time report
9:di Huly langsung lewat percakapan — tanpa perlu buka dashboard.
10:
11:Satu binary, dua mode:
12:
13:- **stdio (default, personal)** — MCP client (Claude Code, Cursor, dst.)
14:  memspawn proses ini; kredensial Huly per-orang lewat env. Target rilis:
15:  package npm di GitLab private kantor, dipakai agent via `npx`.
16:- **http (shared)** — server HTTP stateless bersama di kantor dengan
17:  bearer token + Keycloak OIDC, atribusi per-orang.
18:
19:Project ini berdiri sendiri di `mcp-huly/`, terpisah dari `dashboard-huly`
20:(dashboard KPI internal berbasis Next.js) dan `huly-selfhost` (deployment
21:Huly sendiri).
22:
23:## Kenapa dibuat
24:
25:Sebelum ini, tim mengambil data Huly lewat dashboard web (read-only, untuk
26:laporan/KPI). Yang belum ada: cara cepat untuk Claude membaca *atau
27:mengubah* data Huly secara langsung — misalnya "buatkan issue baru di
28:project X", "update status issue PROJ-123 jadi Done", "siapa saja yang
29:overdue minggu ini". `mcp-huly` mengisi celah itu sebagai server MCP
30:mandiri yang bisa didaftarkan ke Claude Code / Claude Desktop mana pun,
31:tidak terikat ke satu sesi kerja.
32:
33:## Target pengguna
34:
35:Tim internal QTI yang punya akses ke workspace Huly `huly.qti.co.id`, lewat
36:Claude yang dikonfigurasi untuk connect ke server ini (stdio personal, atau
37:endpoint HTTP bersama).
38:
39:## Scope
40:
41:### In scope (sudah diimplementasi)
42:
43:| Entitas | Operasi |
44:|---|---|
45:| Project | list, get, update (nama/deskripsi), archive/unarchive |
46:| Issue | list, get, create, update, delete |
47:| Milestone (sprint) | list, create, update, delete |
48:| Teamspace | list |
49:| Document (wiki) | list, get, create, update, delete |
50:| Test Management (Beta) | list test project/case/run, get run, set result, link issue |
51:| Team member | list (nama + email) |
52:| Time report | list, tambah |
53:
54:Detail skema tiap tool ada di `src/tools.ts`; implementasi di
55:`src/huly-client.ts`.
56:
57:### Sengaja di luar scope
58:
59:- **Membuat project baru.** Project di Huly butuh setup project type, task
60:  type, dan status workflow — normalnya lewat wizard UI Huly. Meniru itu
61:  lewat API berisiko menghasilkan project yang setengah-jadi/rusak. Project
62:  dibuat manual di UI, baru dikelola lewat MCP setelah ada.
63:- **Membuat teamspace baru & test project/suite/case/run baru.** Alasan
64:  sama: setup kompleks, lebih aman dari UI.
65:- **Manajemen user/permission workspace.** Di luar tujuan awal (fokus ke
66:  project management data, bukan admin workspace).
67:- **Notifikasi/webhook dari Huly ke Claude.** Server ini murni request-
68:  response (Claude yang inisiasi), belum ada jalur sebaliknya.
69:
70:## Arsitektur
71:
72:```
73:Mode stdio (personal):
74:  Claude Code / Cursor ──spawn──> mcp-huly (stdio) ──WebSocket──> Huly transactor
75:                                   (env: HULY_URL/WORKSPACE + token ATAU
76:                                    email/password login, ops.
77:                                    HULY_ALLOWED_PROJECTS)
78:
79:Mode HTTP (kantor):
80:  Claude ──HTTPS + Bearer──> mcp-huly (Express) ──WebSocket──> Huly transactor
81:                              (auth: tokens.json statis ATAU JWT Keycloak
82:                               → huly-identities.json → token Huly personal)

# mcp-huly — Project Overview

## Ringkasan

`mcp-huly` adalah MCP (Model Context Protocol) server yang menjembatani
Claude (atau MCP client lain) dengan instance Huly self-hosted milik QTI
(`huly.qti.co.id`). Tujuannya: memungkinkan Claude membaca dan mengelola
project, issue, milestone, document, test run, anggota tim, dan time report
di Huly langsung lewat percakapan — tanpa perlu buka dashboard.

Satu binary, dua mode:

- **stdio (default, personal)** — MCP client (Claude Code, Cursor, dst.)
  memspawn proses ini; kredensial Huly per-orang lewat env. Target rilis:
  package npm di GitLab private kantor, dipakai agent via `npx`.
- **http (shared)** — server HTTP stateless bersama di kantor dengan
  bearer token + Keycloak OIDC, atribusi per-orang.

Project ini berdiri sendiri di `mcp-huly/`, terpisah dari `dashboard-huly`
(dashboard KPI internal berbasis Next.js) dan `huly-selfhost` (deployment
Huly sendiri).

## Kenapa dibuat

Sebelum ini, tim mengambil data Huly lewat dashboard web (read-only, untuk
laporan/KPI). Yang belum ada: cara cepat untuk Claude membaca *atau
mengubah* data Huly secara langsung — misalnya "buatkan issue baru di
project X", "update status issue PROJ-123 jadi Done", "siapa saja yang
overdue minggu ini". `mcp-huly` mengisi celah itu sebagai server MCP
mandiri yang bisa didaftarkan ke Claude Code / Claude Desktop mana pun,
tidak terikat ke satu sesi kerja.

## Target pengguna

Tim internal QTI yang punya akses ke workspace Huly `huly.qti.co.id`, lewat
Claude yang dikonfigurasi untuk connect ke server ini (stdio personal, atau
endpoint HTTP bersama).

## Scope

### In scope (sudah diimplementasi)

| Entitas | Operasi |
|---|---|
| Project | list, get, update (nama/deskripsi), archive/unarchive |
| Issue | list, get, create, update, delete |
| Milestone (sprint) | list, create, update, delete |
| Teamspace | list |
| Document (wiki) | list, get, create, update, delete |
| Test Management (Beta) | list test project/case/run, get run, set result, link issue |
| Team member | list (nama + email) |
| Time report | list, tambah |

Detail skema tiap tool ada di `src/tools.ts`; implementasi di
`src/huly-client.ts`.

### Sengaja di luar scope

- **Membuat project baru.** Project di Huly butuh setup project type, task
  type, dan status workflow — normalnya lewat wizard UI Huly. Meniru itu
  lewat API berisiko menghasilkan project yang setengah-jadi/rusak. Project
  dibuat manual di UI, baru dikelola lewat MCP setelah ada.
- **Membuat teamspace baru & test project/suite/case/run baru.** Alasan
  sama: setup kompleks, lebih aman dari UI.
- **Manajemen user/permission workspace.** Di luar tujuan awal (fokus ke
  project management data, bukan admin workspace).
- **Notifikasi/webhook dari Huly ke Claude.** Server ini murni request-
  response (Claude yang inisiasi), belum ada jalur sebaliknya.

## Arsitektur

```
Mode stdio (personal):
  Claude Code / Cursor ──spawn──> mcp-huly (stdio) ──WebSocket──> Huly transactor
                                   (env: HULY_URL/WORKSPACE + token ATAU
                                    email/password login, ops.
                                    HULY_ALLOWED_PROJECTS)

Mode HTTP (kantor):
  Claude ──HTTPS + Bearer──> mcp-huly (Express) ──WebSocket──> Huly transactor
                              (auth: tokens.json statis ATAU JWT Keycloak
                               → huly-identities.json → token Huly personal)
```

- **Transport stdio**: `StdioServerTransport`; stdout hanya untuk protokol
  JSON-RPC, semua log ke stderr. Satu `HulyService` per proses, shutdown
  bersih saat SIGINT/SIGTERM/stdin ditutup.
- **Transport HTTP**: Streamable HTTP stateless — tiap request membuat
  `McpServer` + transport baru, tidak ada session di memori; lebih sederhana
  dioperasikan dan di-scale (tanpa sticky session).
- **Auth HTTP dua lapis**: `MCP_SERVER_TOKEN` kini digantikan token statis
  di `tokens.json` (scope `all`/`limited` per project identifier) — bearer
  token yang dikirim client; `HULY_API_TOKEN`/login — kredensial server ke
  Huly.
- **Koneksi ke Huly**: `HulyService` singleton per proses (stdio) atau per
  caller token (http), reconnect otomatis sekali kalau request gagal; crash
  guard untuk bug msgpackr/RPC (proses tetap hidup, koneksi di-invalidasi).
- **File layout**:
  - `src/index.ts` — entrypoint, pilih transport (`--http` /
    `MCP_TRANSPORT`, default stdio).
  - `src/config.ts` — validasi env terpusat, resolve kredensial, parse
    `HULY_ALLOWED_PROJECTS`.
  - `src/login.ts` — email/password → token workspace via account API.
  - `src/transports/stdio.ts`, `src/transports/http.ts` — masing-masing
    mode.
  - `src/huly-client.ts` — semua logic koneksi & CRUD + enforcement scope.
  - `src/tools.ts` — registrasi tools MCP (skema zod).

## Keputusan teknis penting

- **Dua mode, satu binary.** stdio dipilih sebagai default karena MCP
  client personal memang memspawn proses (tidak ada endpoint yang perlu
  diamankan — identitas dari env milik user). HTTP tetap dipertahankan
  untuk deployment bersama + Keycloak OIDC (kantor memakai Keycloak,
  jadi verifikasi JWT itu memang kebutuhan nyata, bukan bonus).
- **Kredensial email/password (baru).** Token sesi browser
  (`HULY_API_TOKEN`) expired dan harus di-scrape manual dari URL websocket —
  sumber gangguan operasional utama. Sekarang server bisa login sendiri
  (`HULY_EMAIL`/`HULY_PASSWORD`) lewat account API resmi:
  `loadServerConfig(url).ACCOUNTS_URL` → `AccountClient.login(email,
  password)` → `selectWorkspace(workspace)` → token workspace.
- **"Limited project" = project identifier.** Pembatasan scope
  (`HULY_ALLOWED_PROJECTS` di stdio; `scope: limited` + `-p PROJ-A` di
  tokens/identities untuk HTTP) memakai *project identifier* Huly — kode
  pendek di ID issue (`PROJ` di `PROJ-123`). Enforcement di level query
  `HulyService` (setiap list/get/create memfilter & memvalidasi), bukan
  sekadar menyembunyikan dari list. Akses di luar scope menghasilkan error
  eksplisit yang menyebutkan daftar project yang diizinkan, dan server
  mengirim `instructions` MCP saat handshake supaya agent tahu scope-nya
  sejak awal — bukan "not found" yang membingungkan.
- **Versi paket `@hcengineering/*` di-pin persis**, disalin dari
  `dashboard-huly/package-lock.json` (lewat `overrides` di `package.json`).
  Alasan: beberapa paket Huly (tracker, contact, task, ui, ...) membawa
  salinan `@hcengineering/core` masing-masing dengan versi berbeda-beda
  kalau di-resolve bebas oleh npm, menyebabkan konflik tipe TypeScript.
- **Wrapper `any`-typed di sekitar `PlatformClient`** (`findAll`, `findOne`,
  `createDoc`, dst di `huly-client.ts`) + interface lokal `*Raw` untuk tiap
  entitas. Ini menghindari kebutuhan generic inference yang rewel dari SDK
  Huly, dengan tetap menjaga bentuk data yang benar-benar kita baca/tulis
  jelas dan terketik.
- **Import paket Huly pakai `import x from '...'` (default import) lalu
  destructure**, bukan named import langsung. Build paket-paket ini CJS,
  dan Node ESM loader tidak selalu mendeteksi named export lewat
  `cjs-module-lexer` dengan benar — named import bisa gagal saat runtime
  meskipun lolos type-check.
- **`rank` (LexoRank) & nomor urut issue** dihitung manual saat
  `huly_create_issue`, mengikuti pola resmi Huly: increment
  `project.sequence` via `$inc`, lalu `makeRank(lastIssue?.rank, undefined)`
  dari `@hcengineering/rank`.

## Status saat ini

- [x] Server MCP jalan dalam dua mode (stdio & stateless HTTP).
- [x] 30 tools terdaftar, termasuk claim issue dan delivery record; build
      TypeScript bersih.
- [x] Login email/password (account API) — tidak lagi bergantung token
      browser yang expired.
- [x] `bin` npm + `.gitlab-ci.yml` (build + publish tag `v*` ke Package
      Registry via `CI_JOB_TOKEN`).
- [ ] Smoke test end-to-end dengan kredensial Huly asli (init/tools/list
      sudah; panggilan tool yang benar-benar hit Huly perlu diverifikasi).

## Roadmap / open items

1. Verifikasi end-to-end per tool terhadap `huly.qti.co.id` (list projects,
   create issue, set test result, dll).
2. Publish rilis pertama: `npm version patch && git push --follow-tags`,
   lalu konfigurasi `~/.npmrc` + `npx` di mesin tiap anggota tim (README).
3. Deploy mode HTTP di belakang reverse proxy (nginx/Caddy) dengan TLS di
   server yang sama dengan `huly-selfhost` — hanya jika tim memilih jalur
   server bersama daripada stdio personal.
4. Evaluasi tools tambahan (comment, attachment, sub-issue) setelah dipakai
   beberapa minggu.

## Cara jalankan (ringkas)

```bash
npm install
cp .env.example .env   # HULY_URL, HULY_WORKSPACE + kredensial (token ATAU email/password)
npm run build
npm start              # stdio (dipakai MCP client personal)
npm run start:http     # HTTP (deployment bersama)
```

Detail lengkap: `README.md`.

description: "mcp-huly docker container is crash-looping (msgpackr RPC error) and user hit a weird failure updating issue status to \"In Progress\""
metadata:

Two related open issues found 2026-09-03/05:

1. **Container crash-loop**: `mcp-huly` docker container (image `mcp-huly-mcp-huly`) is in a
   restart loop — RestartCount was 16 and climbing. Docker reports it "healthy" because the
   healthcheck just probes port 12345 right after boot, before it crashes again. Each cycle:
   - boots, logs `[mcp-huly] MCP server listening on http://0.0.0.0:12345/mcp`
   - floods `no document found, failed to apply model transaction, skipping ... TxUpdateDoc
     objectId=...` (stale transactions referencing objects that no longer exist in the model)
   - then fatally throws:
     ```
     Error: Data read, but end of buffer not reached 112
         at checkedRead (msgpackr/dist/node.cjs:218:10)
         at RPCHandler.readResponse (@hcengineering/rpc/lib/rpc.js:127:23)
     ```
     — a websocket RPC payload from the Huly server fails to deserialize with msgpackr —
     process exits, docker restarts it, loop repeats.
   - Suspected cause: protocol drift between the pinned `@hcengineering` client version
     (see [[mcp-huly-hcengineering-version-pin]], pinned at 0.7.382) and whatever the live
     Huly server is actually running now. Not yet confirmed — need to check live server
     version vs 0.7.382.

2. **Status update to "In Progress" fails ("aneh"/weird error)**: user could update
   description and priority on an issue fine, but setting status to "In Progress" failed,
   even though that exact status is valid and used by other issues in the same project.
   - Code path: `updateIssue()` in `mcp-huly/src/huly-client.ts` (~line 698-705) does
     `findOne(client, tracker.class.IssueStatus, { space: issue.space, name: updates.statusName })`
     and throws `No issue status named '...' found in this project` if nothing matches.
   - Logic itself looks correct/simple; leading theory is the crash-loop above is actually
     the cause — the RPC connection dies mid-request during the status update, producing a
     transport-level error that looks unrelated to the (valid) status name, rather than a
     real "status not found" logic bug.
   - Not yet confirmed: still need the exact error text the user saw, and/or a live
     reproduction with `docker logs -f mcp-huly` tailing while retrying the update.

**Next steps when resuming**: get exact error text from user, or restart the container and
watch logs live while reproducing the status update, to determine whether this is the same
root cause as the crash-loop or a separate logic bug in `updateIssue`.

**New repro data (2026-09-07)**, found incidentally while testing the new document tools
([[mcp-huly-document-feature]]) with a short-lived `tsx` script (not the long-running docker
container) against the live server: the same "Data read, but end of buffer not reached 112"
msgpackr crash reproduces reliably right after a mutating call (`createDoc`/`removeDoc`), but
NOT deterministically on the mutating call's own response - once it hit mid-`removeDoc` (that
call's promise never resolved, though the deletion still landed server-side), another time the
mutating call completed and returned normally and the crash hit on the *next* unrelated call
(a subsequent `listDocuments`) instead. This points toward an out-of-band push (a live-update/
notification broadcast the server sends after any write) arriving on the same websocket and
corrupting the RPC handler's read state for whatever request happens to be in flight next -
not a bug tied to any specific mcp-huly tool or entity type. Reinforces the existing "protocol
drift vs. live server" theory over an issue-specific logic bug.

**Production severity confirmed (2026-09-07, same session)**: end-to-end tested the new
document tools through the actual deployed container (HTTP `/mcp` endpoint, not a direct
script) - create → get → delete. Every single mutating call (`huly_create_document`,
`huly_delete_document`) crashed the container with the same msgpackr error; it auto-restarted
each time (`restart: unless-stopped`) and the in-flight response still reached the client
correctly before the process died, so results were not wrong - but restart count climbed from
4 to 9 within a handful of calls. This is much worse than the earlier direct-script test (one
crash across ~8 calls). Leading theory: `src/index.ts`'s `/mcp` handler creates a **brand new
HulyService/websocket connection per HTTP request** (stateless design, see `createServer()` in
index.ts) - so every single tool call replays the full stale-transaction backlog ("no document
found, failed to apply model transaction...") from scratch on a fresh connection, which likely
raises the odds of hitting the msgpackr deserialization bug compared to one long-lived
connection reused across many calls (as the direct-script tests did). Worth trying a
longer-lived/pooled connection (or at least reusing one HulyService per token across requests)
as a mitigation, separate from actually fixing the root protocol-drift cause.

**Confirmed also hits plain reads, not just mutations (2026-09-08)**: user
reported an error on `huly_list_issues` ("get task list"). Live server
`/config.json` still reports `MODEL_VERSION 0.7.301` / `VERSION 0.7.310`
(unchanged since 2026-09-03) against client pin `0.7.382` - drift confirmed,
not a version change on the server side. `RestartCount` had climbed to 23.
Root mechanism nailed down precisely: the msgpackr throw happens inside
`wsocket.onmessage` in `@hcengineering/client-resources`, which is *outside*
any request's promise chain - so it's an uncaught exception that kills the
whole Node process, not something `tools.ts`'s per-tool try/catch can ever
catch. Compounded by `src/index.ts` building a brand-new `HulyService` (and
thus a brand-new websocket + full stale-tx-backlog replay) on literally
every `/mcp` HTTP request (see the `createServer()` call inside the POST
handler, stateless-transport pattern) - each call was a fresh roll of the
dice.

**Mitigation shipped 2026-09-08** (not a root-cause fix - protocol drift
still stands and the crash still happens in logs, see below):
1. `src/index.ts`: `HulyService` instances are now cached per caller token
   in a module-level `serviceCache` Map (`getHulyService()`), reused across
   requests instead of one-per-request. `HulyService.invalidate()` (new
   method in `huly-client.ts`) drops a cached client's connection without
   trying a graceful `close()` (which could itself throw on an
   already-broken socket).
2. `src/index.ts`: global `process.on('uncaughtException'/'unhandledRejection')`
   handler logs and does **not** exit; when the error text matches the known
   transport signature (`Data read, but end of buffer not reached|msgpackr|
   RPCHandler`) it invalidates every cached `HulyService` so the next call
   transparently reconnects, then keeps serving.

Found 2026-09-08 while filling in the "QA" Huly document (Koperasi teamspace,
id `6a98f415064f7c56b5489e13`) with a test plan/test case draft, on top of
[[mcp-huly-crashloop-and-status-update-bug]] and [[mcp-huly-markup-update-bug]].

**Root bug**: `client.fetchMarkup()` (the public method on `PlatformClient`
from `@hcengineering/api-client`) can return `''` indefinitely for a markup
field that demonstrably has real content - verified side-by-side: calling
`collaborator-client`'s own `getMarkup()` for the exact same
objectClass+objectId+objectAttr, at the same moment, returned the correct
content (thousands of characters). Not a timing race - reproduced reading
`''` repeatedly over 5+ seconds via independent `huly_get_document` calls.
This was silently making `Document.content`, `Issue.description`, and
`TestCase`/`TestResult.description` reads look empty in mcp-huly whenever
this happened - no error, just wrong (empty) data returned.

**Fix**: `fetchMarkup()` in `src/huly-client.ts` now goes through the same
collaborator service `updateMarkupContent()` already writes through
(`collab.getMarkup()`), converting the returned "Markup" JSON string back to
markdown manually (`markupToMarkdown(markupToJSON(markup), {refUrl,
imageUrl})` - `markupToJSON` from `@hcengineering/text`, `markupToMarkdown`
from `@hcengineering/text-markdown`), since collab.getMarkup() returns raw
Markup format, not converted markdown like `client.fetchMarkup(..., 'markdown')`
did. Affects `serializeDocument`, `serializeIssue`, and the shared
`readMarkup()` helper (used by `serializeTestCase`/`serializeTestResult`/
`appendNoteLine`).

**Two more bugs found and fixed in the same pass** (same commit, same
session): (1) `uploadMarkup()`/`createContent` 500s if the collaborator
server has ever seen an objectId+attr before, even if the DB field was since
cleared to null - `updateIssue`/`updateDocument`/`setTestResult` used to
branch on whether the field "looked" empty and wrongly fall back to
`uploadMarkup()` in that case; now always use `updateMarkup()+createMarkup()`
(`updateMarkupContent()`), verified to upsert safely even for a
never-touched objectId. (2) `updateDocument`/`updateIssue` used to
re-`findOne()` right after writing, which could return the pre-write doc;
fixed by using `updateDoc`'s own `retrieve: true` response or merging the
patch locally instead, and passing the markdown just written straight into
the serializer instead of reading it back at all.

**Shipped**: commit `a7bca0c` on branch `fix/mcp-crash-guard` (same branch as
the crash-guard mitigation, pushed, not yet merged/PR'd as of 2026-09-08).
Verified against the production container: independent `huly_get_document`
now returns real markdown for a field that read empty before the fix;
`huly_list_issues` descriptions read correctly including embedded image
links; update-then-reread round-trips work without the old 500s.

**Open question**: whether this class of `client.fetchMarkup()` unreliability
is itself downstream of the same `@hcengineering` client (0.7.382) vs. live
server (model 0.7.301) protocol drift documented in
[[mcp-huly-hcengineering-version-pin]] - not confirmed, but consistent with
that theory given fetchMarkup and the msgpackr crash both live in the
client/server RPC path.

In `mcp-huly` (and likely `dashboard-huly`, untested there), the
`@hcengineering/*` npm packages must stay pinned to **0.7.382** in
`package.json` dependencies + `overrides` — not `latest` (0.7.423 at time of
writing).

**Why:** npm releases 0.7.411 and later (including 0.7.423) ship a
`package.json` with `"types": "types/index.d.ts"` but the `types/` folder is
missing from the published tarball — verified with `npm pack` + `tar tzf`.
TypeScript build fails with `TS7016: Could not find a declaration file`
across the whole SDK. 0.7.382 (published 2026-03-16) is the newest version
confirmed to have working type declarations for all the packages mcp-huly
uses (core, api-client, tracker, contact, attachment, rank,
collaborator-client, client-resources, text, text-markdown).

Exceptions that don't have a 0.7.382 release and must stay at 0.7.423
(they're not directly imported by mcp-huly's TS code, so missing types
don't matter): `@hcengineering/activity`, `@hcengineering/card`,
`@hcengineering/time`.

**Why pinning matters at all:** the self-hosted Huly server's RPC/msgpackr
wire protocol drifts between releases. Client packages too far behind the
server (was 0.7.17-23 vs. a v0.7.310 server) crash the whole Node process
on almost any operation: `Error: Data read, but end of buffer not reached`
in `msgpackr` / `RPCHandler.protoDeserialize`, uncaught, kills the process
(Docker restarts it, dropping in-flight MCP requests). Confirmed by
reproducing the crash before the version bump, and confirming it stopped
after pinning to 0.7.382 - re-verify server version and possibly bump this
pin again if the crash resurfaces.

metadata:

In Huly's `@hcengineering/api-client`, `client.uploadMarkup()` (which wraps
`collaborator-client`'s `createMarkup()`) only **initializes** a
collaborative markup document for a given `objectClass+objectId+objectAttr`.
If a doc already exists there (e.g. an Issue already has a non-empty
`description`), calling `uploadMarkup()` again with new text silently
**ignores the new content** and just re-snapshots whatever is already live
— it returns a fresh-looking `MarkupBlobRef` and the write "succeeds" (no
error, `modifiedOn` bumps), but the field's actual content never changes.
Verified empirically with a debug script directly against the live
transactor + collaborator service.

This was the root cause of a real bug in mcp-huly's `updateIssue`: calling
it with a new `description` looked successful but the old text stayed, and
in the Huly web client this manifested as the description panel spinning
forever (likely because of the resulting inconsistent blob-ref state).

**Fix:** to actually change an existing markup field, call
`collaborator-client`'s `updateMarkup(collabId, markup)` first (NOT exposed
on the public `PlatformClient` — must construct a `CollaboratorClient`
directly via `getClient(workspace, token, COLLABORATOR_URL)`, with
`COLLABORATOR_URL` from `loadServerConfig(url)`), then call `createMarkup()`
again to get a fresh `MarkupBlobRef` reflecting the update, and store THAT
ref on the document. `uploadMarkup()`/`createMarkup()` alone is only correct
for a field's first-ever write (e.g. issue creation with a description).

Implemented in mcp-huly as `updateMarkupContent()` in `src/huly-client.ts`,
used conditionally in `updateIssue()`: first-write path still uses plain
`uploadMarkup()`, but a field that already has content uses the
`updateMarkup()`+`createMarkup()` sequence instead.

Huly has no OIDC login (`@hcengineering/account-client` only supports
`login(email, password)`/OTP), so `HULY_API_TOKEN` in mcp-huly's `.env` is
always one personal session token — every create/update/delete via MCP is
attributed in Huly (`createdBy`/`modifiedBy`) to whichever account owns
that one token, regardless of which MCP client or `MCP_SERVER_TOKEN` called
it. This came up because the user's dev team noticed all MCP-created issues
showed the user's own account as creator.

Implemented (commit `36270b5`, local-only as of 2026-09-03 — push blocked
by a DNS outage in the sandbox, see [[mcp-huly-push-pending]]) an opt-in
two-layer fix:
1. `src/oidc.ts` — verifies a Keycloak JWT via JWKS (reuses
   `dashboard-huly`'s Keycloak realm, `https://keycloak.qti.co.id/realms/huly`).
   No-op unless `OIDC_ISSUER` env is set — default behavior (static tokens
   from `tokens.json` only) is unchanged when unconfigured.
2. `src/huly-identities.ts` + `huly-identities.json` — maps the verified
   OIDC email to that person's own personal Huly API token (managed via
   `npm run token -- identity set/list/check/remove`). OIDC only proves
   *who's calling*; this mapping is what actually decides which Huly
   account the request connects as.

`/mcp` middleware order: try static token in `tokens.json` first (uses the
shared `HULY_API_TOKEN`) → else try OIDC JWT verification → if valid but
email has no registered identity, 403 with the exact `identity set` command
to fix it (never silently falls back to the shared token) → else 401.

Verified: forged-signature JWT correctly rejected (401), static-token path
unaffected with OIDC on or off, identity CLI round-trips. Full design
rationale and setup steps are in mcp-huly's own `README.md` ("Identitas
akun Huly" section) — that's the source of truth going forward, not this
memory.

A channel is an MCP server that pushes events into your running Claude Code session, so Claude can react to things that happen while you're not at the terminal. Channels can be two-way: Claude reads the event and replies back through the same channel, like a chat bridge.
You install a channel as a plugin and configure it with your own credentials. Telegram, Discord, and iMessage are included in the research preview.
When Claude replies through a channel, you see the inbound message in your terminal but not the reply text.
Each supported channel is a plugin that requires Bun. For a hands-on demo of the plugin flow before connecting a real platform, try the fakechat quickstart.
View the full [Telegram plugin source](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-plugins-official/tree/main/external_plugins/telegram).

Each channel plugin is a Bun subprocess running an MCP server over stdio transport. Claude Code launches the plugin, which connects outbound to the messaging platform (no inbound ports needed).
Messaging App (Mobile/Desktop)
| (Platform API — outbound polling or WebSocket)
Channel Plugin (Bun subprocess, MCP Server)
| (stdio transport, MCP protocol)
Claude Code Session (local, full filesystem access)
Key Components
server.ts
The core of each channel plugin. Handles:
* Platform connection: Telegram via HTTP long-polling, Discord via WebSocket Gateway
* STATE_DIR resolution: process.env.<CHANNEL>_STATE_DIR ?? ~/.claude/channels/<channel>
* Access gating: Every inbound message passes through gate() before reaching Claude
* MCP tool registration: Exposes reply, react, edit_message, etc.
skills/access/SKILL.md
A prompt-based skill (not executable code) that Claude reads and follows. Manages:
* No args: display current status (token masked, policy, allowlist count)
* With token: write to <STATE_DIR>/.env with chmod 600
* clear: remove token from .env
plugin.json
Declares the MCP tools, channel capability, and metadata:
{
"name": "discord",
"description": "Discord channel for Claude Code",
"capabilities": {
"experimental": { "claude/channel": {} }
}
}
MCP Tools
* Tool | Discord | Telegram | Description
* reply | Yes | Yes | Send message (auto-chunks, supports file attach)
* react | Yes | Yes | Add emoji reaction
* edit_message | Yes | Yes | Edit bot's own message
* fetch_messages | Yes | No | Pull recent history (1-100 messages)
* download_attachment | Yes | Yes | Download files to inbox/
Key differences
* Discord reply: max 2000 chars/chunk, 25MB/file, 10 files max
* Telegram reply: max 4096 chars/chunk, 50MB/file, supports MarkdownV2 format, supports inline keyboard buttons (buttons param — local fork)
* Discord has fetch_messages for channel history lookback; Telegram has no equivalent
Access Control (access.json)
Schema
Gate Flow
Every inbound message is processed by gate():
1. deliver — message passes through to Claude Code
2. drop — silently ignored (unauthorized sender or disabled policy)
3. pair — bot replies with pairing code (max 2 replies, then silent)
  Rate limits in pairing mode:
* Max 2 replies per pending code (initial + 1 reminder)
* Max 3 pending codes simultaneously
* Codes expire after 1 hour
File handling
start.sh exports <CHANNEL>_STATE_DIR to project-level paths:
export DISCORD_STATE_DIR=$PROJECT_DIR/.claude/channels/discord
export TELEGRAM_STATE_DIR=$PROJECT_DIR/.claude/channels/telegram
The server respects this:
const STATE_DIR = process.env.DISCORD_STATE_DIR
?? join(homedir(), '.claude', 'channels', 'discord')

sources.snippet:
* Claude Pro or Max subscription: log in with your Claude.ai account. Subscribe at claude.com/pricing.
* Claude for Teams or Enterprise: log in with the Claude.ai account your team admin invited you to.
* Claude Console: log in with your Console credentials. Your admin must have invited you first.
You can sign in with or without creating an API key.
* Cloud providers: if your organization uses Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, or Microsoft Foundry, set the required environment variables before running claude, or select 3rd-party platform at the login prompt, which launches an interactive setup wizard for Bedrock and Vertex AI.
No browser login is needed.
* Cloud gateway: if your organization runs a self-hosted Claude apps gateway, sign in with corporate SSO through /login. The gateway-issued token is the session's only credential.
Each invited user needs to:
* Accept the Console invite
* [Check system requirements](/docs/en/setup#system-requirements)
* [Install Claude Code](/docs/en/setup#install-claude-code)
* Log in with Console account credentials
* Sign in with your Console account, labeled (recommended): Claude Code keeps the OAuth token from that sign-in and stores it as an Anthropic profile. It creates no API key
* Create an API key, labeled (legacy): Claude Code creates a Console API key for you and stores it with your other credentials
Developers can log in from several paths: the terminal /login flow, the VS Code extension, the Agent SDK, claude setup-token, /install-github-app, and gateway sign-in for organizations that route through a cloud gateway. On Claude Code v2.1.212 or later, every path applies forceLoginMethod; before v2.1.212, only terminal logins applied either key.
* Terminal, VS Code extension, and Agent SDK logins: verify forceLoginOrgUUID for claude.ai account logins
* claude setup-token and /install-github-app: enforce only forceLoginMethod, so they can mint a token in a different organization
* ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, or apiKeyHelper: blocked at startup, since organization membership can't be verified for an environment credential
* Cloud provider sessions such as Amazon Bedrock: not blocked, because they authenticate against your cloud provider. Restrict those through your cloud IAM policies
apiKeyHelper, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, and ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN apply to the CLI and the surfaces that wrap it, including the VS Code extension, the Agent SDK, and GitHub Actions.
Claude Desktop and cloud sessions do not call apiKeyHelper or read these environment variables: they use OAuth, except desktop sessions running a third-party inference configuration, which authenticate with that configuration's credential.
It does not save the token anywhere; copy it and set it as the CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN environment variable wherever you want to authenticate:
export CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN=your-token
This token authenticates with your Claude subscription and requires a Pro, Max, Team, or Enterprise plan.

* OAuth Token (Max subscription): Set CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN environment variable
Authentication

Method 1: API Key (Pay-as-you-go Plans)

export CLAUDE_API_KEY=your-api-key-here

claude setup-token

2. Export the token to your environment:
export CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN=your-oauth-token-here

# Push events into a running session with channels

> Use channels to push messages, alerts, and webhooks into your Claude Code session from an MCP server. Forward CI results, chat messages, and monitoring events so Claude can react while you're away.

<Note>
  Channels are in [research preview](#research-preview). They require Anthropic authentication through claude.ai or a Console API key, and are not available on Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, or Microsoft Foundry. Team and Enterprise organizations must [explicitly enable them](#enterprise-controls).
</Note>

A channel is an MCP server that pushes events into your running Claude Code session, so Claude can react to things that happen while you're not at the terminal. Channels can be two-way: Claude reads the event and replies back through the same channel, like a chat bridge. Events only arrive while the session is open, so for an always-on setup you run Claude in a background process or persistent terminal.

Unlike integrations that spawn a fresh cloud session or wait to be polled, the event arrives in the session you already have open: see [how channels compare](#how-channels-compare).

You install a channel as a plugin and configure it with your own credentials. Telegram, Discord, and iMessage are included in the research preview.

When Claude replies through a channel, you see the inbound message in your terminal but not the reply text. The terminal shows the tool call and a confirmation (like "sent"), and the actual reply appears on the other platform.

If you manage a Team, Enterprise, or Console organization, see [Enable channels for your organization](#enterprise-controls). To build your own channel, see the [Channels reference](/docs/en/channels-reference).

## Supported channels

Each supported channel is a plugin that requires [Bun](https://bun.sh). For a hands-on demo of the plugin flow before connecting a real platform, try the [fakechat quickstart](#quickstart).

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="Telegram">
    View the full [Telegram plugin source](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-plugins-official/tree/main/external_plugins/telegram).

    <Steps>
      <Step title="Create a Telegram bot">
        Open [BotFather](https://t.me/BotFather) in Telegram and send `/newbot`. Give it a display name and a unique username ending in `bot`. Copy the token BotFather returns.
      </Step>

      <Step title="Install the plugin">
        In Claude Code, run:

        ```
        /plugin install telegram@claude-plugins-official
        ```

        If the install fails, match the message Claude Code reports:

        * `Marketplace "claude-plugins-official" not found`: add the marketplace with `/plugin marketplace add anthropics/claude-plugins-official`, then retry the install.
        * The plugin is [not found in the marketplace](/docs/en/plugins/install#install-a-plugin): check the plugin name.

        When the install asks for an installation scope, choose the user scope option so the plugin is available across all your projects. Check the install summary: if it reports `Run /reload-plugins to activate.`, see [Apply plugin changes without restarting](/docs/en/plugins/cli-reference#reload-plugins) to make the plugin's configure command available.
      </Step>

      <Step title="Configure your token">
        Run the configure command with the token from BotFather:

        ```
        /telegram:configure <token>
        ```

        This saves it to `~/.claude/channels/telegram/.env`. You can also set `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` in your shell environment before launching Claude Code.
      </Step>

      <Step title="Restart with channels enabled">
        Exit Claude Code and restart with the channel flag. This starts the Telegram plugin, which begins polling for messages from your bot:

        ```bash theme={null}
        claude --channels plugin:telegram@claude-plugins-official
        ```
      </Step>

      <Step title="Pair your account">
        Open Telegram and send any message to your bot. The bot replies with a pairing code.

        <Note>If your bot doesn't respond, make sure Claude Code is running with `--channels` from the previous step. The bot can only reply while the channel is active.</Note>

        Back in Claude Code, run:

        ```
        /telegram:access pair <code>
        ```

        Then lock down access so only your account can send messages:

        ```
        /telegram:access policy allowlist
        ```
      </Step>
    </Steps>
  </Tab>

  <Tab title="Discord">
    View the full [Discord plugin source](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-plugins-official/tree/main/external_plugins/discord).

    <Steps>
      <Step title="Create a Discord bot">
        Go to the [Discord Developer Portal](https://discord.com/developers/applications), click **New Application**, and name it. In the **Bot** section, create a username, then click **Reset Token** and copy the token.
      </Step>

      <Step title="Enable Message Content Intent">
        In your bot's settings, scroll to **Privileged Gateway Intents** and enable **Message Content Intent**.
      </Step>

      <Step title="Invite the bot to your server">
        Go to **OAuth2 > URL Generator**. Select the `bot` scope and enable these permissions:

        * View Channels
        * Send Messages
        * Send Messages in Threads
        * Read Message History
        * Attach Files
        * Add Reactions

        Open the generated URL to add the bot to your server.
      </Step>

      <Step title="Install the plugin">
        In Claude Code, run:

        ```
        /plugin install discord@claude-plugins-official
        ```

        If the install fails, match the message Claude Code reports:

        * `Marketplace "claude-plugins-official" not found`: add the marketplace with `/plugin marketplace add anthropics/claude-plugins-official`, then retry the install.
        * The plugin is [not found in the marketplace](/docs/en/plugins/install#install-a-plugin): check the plugin name.

        When the install asks for an installation scope, choose the user scope option so the plugin is available across all your projects. Check the install summary: if it reports `Run /reload-plugins to activate.`, see [Apply plugin changes without restarting](/docs/en/plugins/cli-reference#reload-plugins) to make the plugin's configure command available.
      </Step>

      <Step title="Configure your token">
        Run the configure command with the bot token you copied:

        ```
        /discord:configure <token>
        ```

        This saves it to `~/.claude/channels/discord/.env`. You can also set `DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN` in your shell environment before launching Claude Code.
      </Step>

      <Step title="Restart with channels enabled">
        Exit Claude Code and restart with the channel flag. This connects the Discord plugin so your bot can receive and respond to messages:

        ```bash theme={null}
        claude --channels plugin:discord@claude-plugins-official
        ```
      </Step>

      <Step title="Pair your account">
        DM your bot on Discord. The bot replies with a pairing code.

        <Note>If your bot doesn't respond, make sure Claude Code is running with `--channels` from the previous step. The bot can only reply while the channel is active.</Note>

        Back in Claude Code, run:

        ```
        /discord:access pair <code>
        ```

        Then lock down access so only your account can send messages:

        ```
        /discord:access policy allowlist
        ```
      </Step>
    </Steps>
  </Tab>

  <Tab title="iMessage">
    View the full [iMessage plugin source](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-plugins-official/tree/main/external_plugins/imessage).

    The iMessage channel reads your Messages database directly and sends replies through AppleScript. It requires macOS and needs no bot token or external service.

    <Steps>
      <Step title="Grant Full Disk Access">
        The Messages database at `~/Library/Messages/chat.db` is protected by macOS. The first time the server reads it, macOS prompts for access: click **Allow**. The prompt names whichever app launched Bun, such as Terminal, iTerm, or your IDE.

        If the prompt doesn't appear or you clicked Don't Allow, grant access manually under **System Settings > Privacy & Security > Full Disk Access** and add your terminal. Without this, the server exits immediately with `authorization denied`.
      </Step>

      <Step title="Install the plugin">
        In Claude Code, run:

        ```
        /plugin install imessage@claude-plugins-official
        ```

        If the install fails, match the message Claude Code reports:

        * `Marketplace "claude-plugins-official" not found`: add the marketplace with `/plugin marketplace add anthropics/claude-plugins-official`, then retry the install.
        * The plugin is [not found in the marketplace](/docs/en/plugins/install#install-a-plugin): check the plugin name.

        When the install asks for an installation scope, choose the user scope option so the plugin is available across all your projects.

        If the install summary reports `Run /reload-plugins to activate.`, you don't need to act on it here, because restarting in the next step picks up the plugin.
      </Step>

      <Step title="Restart with channels enabled">
        Exit Claude Code and restart with the channel flag:

        ```bash theme={null}
        claude --channels plugin:imessage@claude-plugins-official
        ```
      </Step>

      <Step title="Text yourself">
        Open Messages on any device signed into your Apple ID and send a message to yourself. It reaches Claude immediately: self-chat bypasses access control with no setup.

        <Note>The first reply Claude sends triggers a macOS Automation prompt asking if your terminal can control Messages. Click **OK**.</Note>
      </Step>

      <Step title="Allow other senders">
        By default, only your own messages pass through. To let another contact reach Claude, add their handle:

        ```
        /imessage:access allow +15551234567
        ```

        Handles are phone numbers in `+country` format or Apple ID emails like `user@example.com`.
      </Step>
    </Steps>
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

## Quickstart

Fakechat is an officially supported demo channel that runs a chat UI on localhost, with nothing to authenticate and no external service to configure.

Once you install and enable fakechat, you can type in the browser and the message arrives in your Claude Code session. Claude replies, and the reply shows up back in the browser. After you've tested the fakechat interface, try out [Telegram](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-plugins-official/tree/main/external_plugins/telegram), [Discord](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-plugins-official/tree/main/external_plugins/discord), or [iMessage](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-plugins-official/tree/main/external_plugins/imessage).

To try the fakechat demo, you'll need:

* Claude Code [installed and authenticated](/docs/en/quickstart#step-1-install-claude-code) with a claude.ai account or a Claude Console API key
* [Bun](https://bun.sh) installed. The pre-built channel plugins are Bun scripts. Check with `bun --version`; if that fails, [install Bun](https://bun.sh/docs/installation).
* **Team, Enterprise, or managed Console org**: your admin must [enable channels](#enterprise-controls) in managed settings

<Steps>
  <Step title="Install the fakechat channel plugin">
    Start a Claude Code session and run the install command:

    ```text theme={null}
    /plugin install fakechat@claude-plugins-official
    ```

    If the install fails, match the message Claude Code reports:

    * `Marketplace "claude-plugins-official" not found`: add the marketplace with `/plugin marketplace add anthropics/claude-plugins-official`, then retry the install.
    * The plugin is [not found in the marketplace](/docs/en/plugins/install#install-a-plugin): check the plugin name.

    When the install asks for an installation scope, choose the user scope option so the plugin is available across all your projects.

    If the install summary reports `Run /reload-plugins to activate.`, you don't need to act on it here, because restarting in the next step picks up the plugin.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Restart with the channel enabled">
    Exit Claude Code, then restart with `--channels` and pass the fakechat plugin you installed:

    ```bash theme={null}
    claude --channels plugin:fakechat@claude-plugins-official
    ```

    The fakechat server starts automatically. The startup screen shows a channels notice stating that messages from `plugin:fakechat@claude-plugins-official` inject directly in this session. If the plugin isn't installed or isn't on the approved allowlist, a warning line naming the problem appears below that notice.

    <Tip>
      You can pass several plugins to `--channels`, space-separated.
    </Tip>
  </Step>

  <Step title="Push a message in">
    Open the fakechat UI at [http://localhost:8787](http://localhost:8787) and type a message:

    ```text theme={null}
    what's in my working directory?
    ```

    The message arrives in your Claude Code session. The terminal shows it as an inbound channel line like `← fakechat · web: what's in my working directory?`, while the model receives it as a `<channel source="plugin:fakechat:fakechat">` event, using the plugin's scoped server name. Claude reads it, does the work, and calls fakechat's `reply` tool. If Claude Code asks for permission for the first reply, approve it. The answer shows up in the chat UI.
  </Step>
</Steps>

If Claude hits a permission prompt while you're away from the terminal, the session pauses until you respond. Channel servers that declare the [permission relay capability](/docs/en/channels-reference#relay-permission-prompts) can forward these prompts to you so you can approve or deny remotely. For unattended use, [`--dangerously-skip-permissions`](/docs/en/permission-modes#skip-all-checks-with-bypasspermissions-mode) bypasses most prompts, but only use it in environments you trust. Even then, the [actions no mode auto-approves](/docs/en/permission-modes#actions-no-mode-auto-approves) still apply.

When you run channels in non-interactive mode with `-p`, tools that need terminal input, such as multiple-choice questions and plan mode approval, are disabled so the session never stalls waiting for input.

## Security

Every approved channel plugin maintains a sender allowlist: only IDs you've added can push messages, and everyone else is silently dropped.

Telegram and Discord bootstrap the list by pairing:

1. Find your bot in Telegram or Discord and send it any message
2. The bot replies with a pairing code
3. In your Claude Code session, approve the code when prompted
4. Your sender ID is added to the allowlist

iMessage works differently: texting yourself bypasses the gate automatically, and you add other contacts by handle with `/imessage:access allow`.

Secara teknis bisa. Tapi kalau botnya dipakai tim management, pakai langganan Claude pribadi lewat CLI melanggar aturan Anthropic, dan akun kamu yang berisiko kena blokir.

## Cara teknisnya
- **Channels (resmi, masih research preview):** Claude Code punya plugin Telegram bawaan. Jalankan `claude --channels plugin:telegram@claude-plugins-official`, maka pesan Telegram masuk ke sesi Claude Code dan dibalas lewat bot. Bisa login pakai akun langganan tanpa API key. WhatsApp tidak termasuk; yang tersedia cuma Telegram, Discord, dan iMessage. [Dokumentasi channels](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels.md)
- **Mode headless:** perintah `claude -p "..." --output-format json --mcp-config ...` dipanggil dari bot buatan sendiri, dan `mcp-huly` bisa dipasang sebagai MCP-nya.

## Kenapa jadi masalah
Bagian "Authentication and credential use" di [halaman legal Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/legal-and-compliance) menyatakan:
- Login OAuth dari langganan Free/Pro/Max hanya untuk pemakaian Claude Code biasa. Anthropic melarang meneruskan permintaan orang lain lewat kredensial Pro/Max ("route requests through Free, Pro, or Max plan credentials on behalf of their users").
- Batas pemakaian Pro/Max dihitung untuk pemakaian perorangan ("assume ordinary, individual usage").
- Anthropic bisa menindak tanpa pemberitahuan.

Kalau management bertanya ke bot dan dijawab pakai langganan kamu, itu masuk kategori "on behalf of users". Selain soal aturan, jatah pemakaian per 5 jam dan mingguan juga akan cepat habis.

Hermes juga tidak bisa jadi jalan pintas. Sejak Februari 2026 Anthropic memblokir token OAuth langganan di aplikasi pihak ketiga ([claude-code#28091](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/28091)). Dukungan langganan Claude di Hermes baru sebatas permintaan fitur ([hermes-agent#25267](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/25267)).

Batasnya:
- **Aman:** bot Telegram yang hanya kamu sendiri pakai. Memang itu tujuan fitur Channels.
- **Tidak aman:** bot yang dipakai banyak orang (management).

## Pilihan yang aman
1. **Claude lewat Vertex AI / Google Cloud.** Tagihannya masuk billing GCP, jadi tidak perlu API key dari Anthropic. Cocok kalau kantor sudah punya akun atau kredit GCP.
2. **API key dari Claude Console,** bayar sesuai pemakaian. Untuk tanya-jawab progres, model kecil (Haiku) biasanya sudah cukup. Tarif per token cek langsung di halaman harga, karena belum saya verifikasi.
3. **Laporan otomatis tanpa LLM.** Kebutuhan "sejauh mana progres" sebagian besar bisa berupa ringkasan terjadwal, misalnya per sprint: issue selesai, yang overdue, jam kerja per orang. Datanya ambil dari PostgreSQL `dashboard-huly` yang sudah disinkronkan, lalu kirim ke grup Telegram tiap hari. Tidak butuh model sama sekali. LLM (opsi 1 atau 2) cukup dipakai untuk pertanyaan bebas.

## Catatan dari proyek yang sudah ada
- **Tool Huly:** `mcp-huly` sudah punya tool yang dibutuhkan (`huly_list_issues`, `huly_list_milestones`, `huly_list_time_reports`, dll). Untuk bot management, buat token `limited` di `tokens.json` dan cukup beri akses baca.
- **Risiko keandalan:** menurut memory proyek, crash msgpackr (versi client 0.7.382 tidak cocok dengan model server 0.7.301) belum benar-benar terselesaikan. Untuk bot yang harus selalu jalan, membaca dari DB `dashboard-huly` lebih stabil daripada lewat websocket Huly langsung.
- **WhatsApp:** jalur resminya WhatsApp Cloud API dari Meta, yang butuh verifikasi bisnis dan berbayar per percakapan. Library tidak resmi seperti Baileys berisiko nomornya diblokir. Telegram jauh lebih mudah untuk tahap awal.

Saran saya: mulai dari Telegram. Pakai opsi 3 untuk laporan rutin, ditambah Claude via Vertex atau API key untuk tanya-jawab. Kalau mau, saya bisa buatkan rancangan arsitektur dan kerangka bot-nya.
